title.narrative: Integrated GBV Prevention and Response for Conflict-Affected Communities in Oromia Region

description.narrative: ltpgtltspangtThe project titled “Integrated GBV Prevention and Response for Conflict-Affected Communities in Oromia Region” is a 10-month humanitarian initiative led by Action Against Hunger (ACF) in partnership with the Ethiopian Evangelical Church Mekane Yesus Development and Social Services Commission (EECMY-DASSC). The project targets four conflict-affected Woredas in Oromia—Gimbi, Boji Dirmeji, Sayo, and Gawo Kebe where internally displaced persons (IDPs) and vulnerable host communities face severe protection risks, particularly women, adolescent girls, children, and persons with disabilities.lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtA total of 25,601 individuals will be directly reached through this intervention, including 10,129 women, 3,876 girls, 7,720 men, and 3,876 boys, of whom 2,048 are persons with disabilities. Action Against Hunger will implement activities in Gimbi and Sayo, reaching 12,801 people, while EECMY-DASSC will serve 12,801 people across two districts, which are Boji Dirmeji and Gawo Kebe. The project is funded with a total budget of USD 650,000, fully dedicated to protection-focused programming.ltbrgtCommunities in the targeted areas have been exposed to widespread conflict and displacement, leading to increased cases of gender-based violence (GBV) such as rape, intimate partner violence, early and forced marriage, and harmful traditional practices including female genital mutilation (FGM). These risks are compounded by limited access to essential services, overstretched health systems, food insecurity, psychosocial distress, and high rates of youth unemployment.ltbrgtThe overarching objective of the project is to provide lifesaving, inclusive GBV protection and MHPSS response services through a survivor-centered and community-based approach. This includes strengthening health and protection systems, building local capacity, and improving access to safe, confidential, and quality support for those affected by violence.ltbrgtKey activities include:ltbrgtlt/pgtltulgtltligtGBV Case Management Mental Health and Psychosocial Support: Delivering tailored services, including case management psychosocial support, emergency cash assistance, and referrals, through a tailored Individual Protection Assistance (IPA) mechanism.lt/ligtltligtHealth Facility Support: Supplying non-medical equipment and sanitary materials to local health centers and the Bureau of Women and Social Affairs (BoWSA) to scale up and deliver comprehensive GBV protection and response services.lt/ligtltligtCapacity Building: Training over 320 frontline workers on Clinical Management of Rape (CMR), Psychological First Aid (PFA), Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA), GBV case management, and inclusion practices.lt/ligtltligtWomen and Girls Safe Spaces (WGSS): Establishing two new and reinforcing two existing WGSS, providing psychosocial services, life-skills activities, and safe environments for more than 8,350 women and girls.lt/ligtltligtDignity Kit Distribution: Distributing 3,000 dignity kits to vulnerable women and girls to support hygiene and personal safety.lt/ligtltligtCommunity Engagement: Conducting consultations and community dialogues to raise awareness on GBV, address harmful practices, and promote inclusive service access.lt/ligtltligtReferral Systems and Monitoring: Strengthening GBV referral pathways, conducting safety audits, and applying accountability and feedback mechanisms throughout the project cycle.lt/ligtlt/ulgtltpgtThis project promotes local ownership by working closely with community-based structures and local authorities. By integrating inclusive, survivor-centered protection services, the proposed action aims to reduce GBV risks, build community resilience, and restore dignity and well-being for those most vulnerable and affected by the ongoing conflict and service deprivation in the Oromia region targeted woredas.ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgt lt/pgt
